title: Weekly dengue cases and satellite exposures, municipalities of Rio de Janeiro state, 2024

licence.note: Stated on the Zenodo record. The boundaries are CC BY 3.0 IGO, stated by geoBoundaries. InfoDengue's own terms, the origin of the counts, were not found.

derivation: Rows of dataset_multimodal_v8.parquet with estado RJ and anio 2024; 19 of 87 columns; read with hyparquet; values as published, data_iniSE written as a date. Boundaries: each of the dataset's 92 municipality names matched exactly to a geoBoundaries ADM2 name, the unit nearest the Rio de Janeiro state outline kept where 2 or 3 units share a name (7 names); coordinates rounded to 6 decimals. The sixteen-year file, data/dengue-rj-2010-2025.csv: the same 19 columns, every row with estado RJ, anio 2010 to 2025, read the same way, ordered by municipality and week.

verification.cases: 426,479 in all rows; 423,795 without the week starting 2024-12-29

findings: SE 202501, the week starting 2024-12-29, appears twice for every municipality, labelled semana 1 and anio 2024; the two rows differ only in precip_total_semana, one of them 0.
LST_Day_mean, LST_Night_mean, NDVI_mean and EVI_mean take 11 or 12 distinct values per municipality over the year: monthly values repeated weekly.
n_pixels is about 438 m² a pixel over Rio de Janeiro city, not MODIS's 1 km; which layer it counts is not stated.
LST_Day_mean is empty in 20 rows and LST_Night_mean in 128.
geoBoundaries' state file spells Rio de Janeiro "Rio de Jeneiro".

In 2010–2025, twelve weeks appear twice for every municipality, each at a year's edge: 2010-12-26, 2011-12-25, 2012-12-30, 2013-12-29, 2015-01-04, 2016-12-25, 2018-12-30, 2019-12-29, 2020-12-27, 2021-12-26, 2022-12-25 and 2024-12-29; 1,104 rows. The two rows agree on cases and differ in precip_total_semana.
The week starting 2014-12-28 has no row for any municipality.

precip_total_semana is CHIRPS v2.0 at the grid cell nearest each municipality's coordinates, summed over ISO weeks (Monday to Sunday), with a missing day counted as 0, as the dataset's repository code builds it (jssanchez-garreta/dataset-multimodal-dengue-brazil, scripts/data_construction/03_build_dataset_precipitacion_chirps_anual.py). That code also refuses a repeated municipality-week, which this file has; the file does not match it.

tempmed is InfoDengue's own column: the dataset's repository code requests it from InfoDengue's alertcity API, one municipality at a time (scripts/data_construction/01_download_infodengue_nacional.py, commit 5c4d30cd01fb17ea44dcbd416d162c272aa92257, read 2026-11-07). InfoDengue's 2015–2016 Rio pilot took temperature from airport weather stations (Codeço et al. 2016, bioRxiv 10.1101/046193); its repository now says climate comes through Mosqlimate from Copernicus ERA5 reanalysis, averaged over each municipality. When the source changed, and whether earlier weeks were recomputed, is not stated.
limits: Notified cases as InfoDengue reports them, not confirmed infections.
How the MODIS columns were computed was not read; tempmed and precip_total_semana are traced in the findings.
